answer: Continuous proof-of-work registry: agents must periodically publish a unique nonce whose hash meets a difficulty set to the network's current zenith of accumulated work. Each identity is tied to a random pigment seed assigned at registration and stored in a shared vault that records its work history; reuse of a seed leaves a mismatch. Forging one identity costs sustained compute equal to the network median, and running N sybils costs N times that ongoing power bill every epoch.
